classification.difficultyReason: Combine divisibility tests with division to generate factor pairs systematically, keeping track of tested candidates so the factor list is complete.

content.prompt: Use the various divisibility tests and short division to help you find all the factors of:

answer.worked:
The digit sum is $1+4+7=12$, so $147$ is divisible by $3$. Division gives $147\div3=49$ and $147\div7=21$.

The factor pairs are $1\times147$, $3\times49$ and $7\times21$. Testing possible smaller factors up to $12$ gives no other pairs, since $12^2<147<13^2$.

The factors are $1, 3, 7, 21, 49, 147$.

The digit sum is $3+4+5=12$, so $345$ is divisible by $3$. Its last digit is $5$, so it is divisible by $5$.

Division gives $345\div3=115$, $345\div5=69$ and $345\div15=23$.

The factor pairs are $1\times345$, $3\times115$, $5\times69$ and $15\times23$. Testing possible smaller factors up to $18$ gives no other pairs, since $18^2<345<19^2$.

The factors are $1, 3, 5, 15, 23, 69, 115, 345$.

The number is even, its digit sum is $24$, its last two digits form $88$, and its last three digits form $688$. Thus it is divisible by $2, 3, 4, 6$ and $8$, but not by $5, 9$ or $10$.

Division gives the following factor pairs:

$$\begin{aligned}2688&=1\times2688\\2688&=2\times1344\\2688&=3\times896\\2688&=4\times672\\2688&=6\times448\\2688&=7\times384\\2688&=8\times336\\2688&=12\times224\\2688&=14\times192\\2688&=16\times168\\2688&=21\times128\\2688&=24\times112\\2688&=28\times96\\2688&=32\times84\\2688&=42\times64\\2688&=48\times56\end{aligned}$$

Testing possible smaller factors up to $51$ gives no other pairs, since $51^2<2688<52^2$.

The factors in order are $1$, $2$, $3$, $4$, $6$, $7$, $8$, $12$, $14$, $16$, $21$, $24$, $28$, $32$, $42$, $48$, $56$, $64$, $84$, $96$, $112$, $128$, $168$, $192$, $224$, $336$, $384$, $448$, $672$, $896$, $1344$, $2688$.
